lesson.menu_title: The Inbox: Read It, Then Decide
lesson.menu_desc: Requests, issues, policy updates and follow-ups -- reading, prioritising and answering in the present tense -- 31 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 3 -- The Inbox: Read It, Then Decide
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Camila Fogaca | Lesson 3 -- The Inbox
lesson.grammar_point: present simple for routine (I need to approve, not I needed to approve)

vocab.title: Match each expression to its meaning
defs: a problem or a situation that needs attention
the day or the time when something must be finished
stopped for now, waiting for something or somebody
a change in a rule, sent to everybody it affects
something a person asks you to do or to approve
something open, waiting for a decision or an answer
a second message to check what happened after the first one

items.situation: A manager asks: "Did you see my request?"
tips: I am going through my inbox right now. Which one is it?
Answer in the present: this is happening now.

items.situation: He asks: "When can you approve it?"
tips: I need the confirmation from finance first. I get back to you by end of day.
get back TO somebody BY a time.

items.situation: He asks: "Why is it still not approved?"
tips: It is on hold until the budget for the quarter is confirmed.

items.situation: The contract problem belongs to another team. What do you say?
tips: That one is with shared services. I follow up on it this morning and I copy you.

items.situation: You send a policy change that needs no answer.
tips: For your information: the policy changes on Monday.
FYI = read it, do not answer it.

items.situation: Describe your routine: what do you do first every morning?
tips: Every morning I go through my inbox before the first meeting.
Routine lives in the present: I go, not I went.

listenings.text: Camila, good morning, it's Claire. Three things before your first meeting. First, the position in Chile. The country manager wrote to me directly, and I need your answer today, by end of day, not tomorrow. Second, the headcount file. I know it is on hold, because finance has not confirmed the budget for the quarter, so please do not spend time on it this week. And third, there is a long message from the works council in my copy to you. That one is only for information. You do not have to answer it, just read it, because it explains what changes in November. That is all. Good luck with the inbox.

Hello Camila, this is the manager of the operations team in Santiago. I am writing, sorry, I am calling, because this is my second message about the same request. I sent the first one on Monday and I did not receive an answer, so this is a follow-up. The situation is simple. One person in my team leaves on the thirtieth, and I need the approval for the replacement before the end of the week. If the problem is the information I sent, tell me. I can send it again in a shorter form, with the cost in one line and the start date in another. Please get back to me when you can. Thank you.
